independent_computation.step_1_both_labels_are_faithful_names: Cached wiki text confirms Black Cleaver's passive is literally named 'Carve' (data/items.json 3071) and Bloodsong's Spellblade inflicts a debuff literally named 'Expose Weakness' (3877). Neither label is fabricated, so 'both_wrong' is not supportable on naming grounds; the question is which effect may legitimately author an entry in a support-event stream.
independent_computation.step_2_effect_domain_separation: The two effects live in different halves of the damage pipeline. Carve is a PERCENT ARMOR REDUCTION (6%/stack, max 30%). Per docs/math-foundations.md §2.2 that is consumed inside reduce_resistance and folded into the mitigation multiplier: R_final = max(0, (R - r_flat)*(1 - r_pct/100)*(1 - p) - f), and the engine's own BC model (§2.3 item 2, §5 audit row 'Terminus/BC ramps') is an AGGREGATE Cesaro-mean constant (0.8*max_stacks), not a per-hit event stream. Expose Weakness is a DAMAGE-TAKEN AMPLIFIER ('take 8%/5% increased damage from all sources') which has no term anywhere in the §2.2 composition; autoresearch-review's E-amp entry confirms amps are a separate stage ('percent -> flat -> amp').

step_3_worked_numbers.carve_full_stacks_vs_100_armor: R = 100 -> 100*(1 - 0.30) = 70 -> m(70) = 100/170 = 0.58824 vs m(100) = 0.50000; effective damage uplift = 0.58824/0.50000 = +17.65%. This uplift is realized ENTIRELY through the resistance term; representing it additionally as a discrete support event would double-count or duplicate state already carried by ArmorReductionEffect.
step_3_worked_numbers.expose_weakness: post-mitigation multiplier x1.08 (melee) / x1.05 (ranged), 4 s duration, >=1.5 s between applications, so at most 1 + floor(T/1.5) applications in a T-second window (e.g. <=7 in a 10 s fight). Being outside the resistance composition, it can only be carried as a discrete, timed, ally-facing event.

independent_computation.step_4_support_channel_membership: In the cached shop data only Bloodsong is SUPPORT-tagged (and it is a Starter/support-quest upgrade, 400g, SR-only); Black Cleaver is a 3000g FIGHTER/ARMOR_PEN legendary in the Fatality group. Bloodsong's Expose Weakness is explicitly 'from all sources', i.e. an ally-facing amplification supplied by the support participant — the canonical support event, and exactly the effect e9-bis-b required to be modeled with authored timing. A Black Cleaver Carve entry in support_events is the documented hazard class autoresearch-review warns about (an actor's own effect routed into the ally-support channel).
independent_computation.step_5_conclusion: For the roster scenario that pairs the two items, the support-event stream should carry Bloodsong's Expose Weakness applications; Black Cleaver's Carve belongs to the target's resistance state (already priced inside m(R)) and not to the support-event stream. The new value is therefore the defensible one at this leaf.

limitations: The exact ordinal (index 17) cannot be reconstructed from the permitted evidence tree: the scenario definition (roster composition, item assignment per participant, fight window, attack speeds) lives in scripts/ and src/, which this runbook forbids reading. The verdict therefore adjudicates WHICH OF THE TWO NAMED SOURCES may legitimately author a support event, not the arithmetic position of the entry.

A purely rate-based prior would favor Carve (it applies once per physical damage instance — data/champions.json: a 5-instance flurry applies 5 stacks — versus Expose Weakness's hard 1.5 s internal cooldown), so if support_events were a raw per-hit debuff log, a late index would more often be Carve. That prior is overridden by step 2/4: under the engine's own documented BC model the shred is an aggregate resistance constant, not an event stream, so a per-hit Carve entry in the support channel is not the modeled behavior.
No claim is made about the numeric fields of support_events[17] (time, amount, magnitude); only the 'source' leaf was adjudicated.
